verbMismatchWhy._what: The PATH resolves, so the path check passes; the handler it resolves to does not export this METHOD, so Next.js answers 405 at runtime and the calling screen swallows it. Shrink-only, like broken[].
verbMismatchWhy._lost_once: These reasons were written on 2026-08-17 and then silently deleted by `audit:api --write-baseline`, which rebuilt the file from three fields. The writer now carries `why` and `verbMismatchWhy` through every rewrite.
verbMismatchWhy.GET /tax/deductions/recommendations: No recommendations route exists, so the call falls through to tax/deductions/[id] with id="recommendations", which exports only PATCH and DELETE. The siblings categories/ and summary/ DO exist with GET; this one was never built. Belongs with the tax-deductions work (tasks #58/#60).
verbMismatchWhy.POST /student-loans: Creating a loan. /api/student-loans exports GET only. Blocked on the same schema decision as the web Add Loan form: student_loans.account_number is NOT NULL and ADR-0013 says store a mask, not a full account number.
verbMismatchWhy.POST /tax/calendar: SCHEMA-BLOCKED, not a missing handler — correcting an earlier note of mine that called this straightforward. createReminder (src/services/api/tax.ts:224) posts a TaxEvent to create a CUSTOM reminder and there is nowhere to put one: the tax_* tables are deductions, documents, profiles, recommendations and strategies, and a search for any event/calendar/deadline table returns only analytics_events, circuit_breaker_events, kill_switch_events, monitoring_events, processed_webhook_events and revenue_events — none a user reminder store. GET does not read a table at all; it COMPUTES the schedule from taxOptimizationEngine.getQuarterlyPaymentSchedule(profile). A POST that answered 200 and stored nothing would be the student-loans Add form defect again. Needs a table decision, in the shape of ADR-0013.
verbMismatchWhy.PATCH /notifications/preferences: NOT a verb typo — do not simply flip it to PUT. The route exports GET and PUT, but mobile types.ts NotificationPreferences carries categories:{disputes,scoreChanges,alerts,recommendations,payments,marketing} while the server model is channels:{dispute_update,score_change,payment_reminder,document_processed,recommendation,system,promotion}, and notification_preferences has NO categories column. Changing the verb alone would persist pushEnabled/emailEnabled/smsEnabled and SILENTLY DROP every category toggle. Exactly the shape proven live on the budgets route: PATCH {amount:750} returned 200 and left the amount at 500.00. Design written up in docs/specs/adr/0014-notification-taxonomy.md (Status: Proposed) — needs D1 (which taxonomy is canonical) and D2 (is the per-category channel matrix real) answered.
verbMismatchWhy.POST /notifications/preferences: app/settings/notification-preferences.tsx sends {categories:[{id,enabled,channels}], quietHours} — a per-category channel MATRIX. The server stores a flat channels object and a quiet_hours object, with no categories column at all. Same reconciliation as the PATCH entry. Design written up in docs/specs/adr/0014-notification-taxonomy.md (Status: Proposed) — needs D1 (which taxonomy is canonical) and D2 (is the per-category channel matrix real) answered.
verbMismatchWhy._disputesFixed: POST /disputes/recommend-strategy closed 2026-08-17. recommendStrategy() already existed in @/lib/disputes/advanced-strategies and was already used by /api/disputes/generate; only the route was missing.
verbMismatchWhy._taxonomy: FIVE notification taxonomies exist in this codebase (push-notification-service, web-push-service+scheduler, the preferences route, mobile types.ts, the mobile settings screen). Only score_change and payment_reminder appear in more than two. notification-scheduler.ts:461 gates delivery on keys the preferences route never writes, so the check is broken at the taxonomy level, not just the transport level. notification_preferences has 0 rows — nobody has ever saved one. See ADR-0014.
verbMismatchWhy.DELETE /financial/accounts/: Disconnecting a bank account (financial.ts:709). The detail route now exists with GET, so this moved from a path break to a verb break — a more accurate description of the same gap. DELETE is deliberately unbuilt: unlinking a Plaid-linked account is destructive with no established pattern here. manual-account-service.deleteAccount() works on `manual_accounts`, a different table, so it is not this. Deleting a financial_accounts row orphans its transactions and discards balance history; the alternative — mark disconnected and revoke the Plaid item — needs a column that does not exist. A DELETE that quietly destroys account history, or one that returns 200 and leaves the account linked, are both worse than the 404 today. Needs a decision on unlink semantics plus, probably, a status column.
